clips.text_zh: 22歲踩中doge，兩年唔做嘢，買咗個condo。之後錢燒晒，返學grad返出嚟，依家27歲做返$100K個工，個condo仲喺度。學費真係貴。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: In 2021 I was 22 and made a bunch of random crypto money from dogecoin. I lived for two years with no job, dropped out of school and bought a condo for $230K. Money ran out, I went back, graduated, and now I make $100K. I'm 27 and stuck in a work-consume loop with student debt and credit card debt.
clips.source_hint: Anon rants about condo regret and the crypto cycle that broke him
clips.text_en_b2: At 22, I struck it lucky with dogecoin and made enough random crypto money to quit everything. I dropped out of school, lived for two years without working, and blew $230K on a condo. When the cash dried up, I went back, finished my degree, and at 27 I'm earning $100K again. The condo is still there, but so is my student debt and credit card debt. I'm caught in a relentless work-consume loop, and tuition was astronomical.
clips.text_en_c1: At twenty-two I stumbled into a windfall from speculative crypto trading, dogecoin of all things, and promptly proceeded to live as though the gravy train would never derail. For two years I neither studied nor worked, eventually sinking $230K into a modest condo whose mortgage I now deeply regret. Once the capital evaporated, I grudgingly returned to university, completed my degree, and at twenty-seven find myself earning a respectable $100K salary, yet mired in a weary work-consume-sleep loop, shackled by student debt and lingering credit card obligations that show no sign of diminishing. Turns out, free money rarely remains free.
clips.text_en_c2: At twenty-two, having struck it lucky on Dogecoin in 2021, I effectively retired for two years, dropped out of university, and blew the proceeds on a $230,000 condominium. Once the windfall evaporated, I grudgingly re-enrolled, finished my degree, and, now twenty-seven, find myself trapped in what can only be described as a Sisyphean work-consume loop. My salary has stabilised at a modest $100,000, yet I remain shackled to the property I so impulsively acquired. Between lingering student loans and accumulated credit-card balances, the arithmetic of that early windfall looks rather less romantic in retrospect. One might be tempted to call it character-building; I would sooner call it a cautionary tale about the perils of liquidity without discipline.

clips.text_zh: 今日pol個邊有條文講Grok個TOS改咗，Elon擺個users嚟做blame shield。又係musk一舉手X又嚟料。睇住TSLA。
clips.text_en_b1: Anons on /pol/ are sharing that Elon changed Grok's TOS so users get blamed when Grok says something people don't like. The drama is blowing up on X, with the rabbi Jeff account posting receipts. Musk keeps rewriting the rules after every controversy.
clips.source_hint: Musk changes Grok TOS, blame shifted to users

signal.rationale: Musk drama = TSLA noise, no setup

clips.text_en_b2: Anons over on /pol/ have dug up a Grok TOS update that conveniently shifts the blame onto users whenever the chatbot spits out something offensive. Musk seems to rewrite the rulebook every time a controversy blows up, and X is once again flooded with drama. The rabbi Jeff account has been posting screenshots as receipts. Meanwhile, TSLA investors are watching closely, wondering whether this is another self-inflicted wound. Given Musk's track record, most anons expect this storm to blow over before it dents the stock.
clips.text_en_c1: Anons over on /pol/ have unearthed an amended Terms of Service governing xAI's Grok, under whose provisions users themselves shoulder culpability whenever the model produces content deemed objectionable by the broader public. Predictably, the controversy has metastasised across X, where the rabbi Jeff account has circulated damning screenshots. Musk, never one to let a scandal pass without intervention, continues to retroactively rewrite the rulebook whenever public sentiment turns hostile, a pattern that has become something of a signature. Tesla investors would do well to monitor the fallout.
clips.text_en_c2: Users on /pol/ have unearthed evidence that Elon Musk has quietly amended Grok's terms of service in a manner that, predictably enough, deflects liability onto ordinary users whenever the model produces content deemed objectionable. The drama, predictably, has metastasised across X, where the @rabbi_jeff account has been diligently posting receipts and inciting the customary pile-on. What is most striking is the cyclical nature of Musk's interventions: every public flare-up begets yet another set of rule revisions, as though governance were merely a reactive subroutine rather than a principled position. Tesla investors, accustomed to such oscillations, are advised to watch the stock with the dispassionate attention one reserves for a slow-motion accident.

clips.text_zh: OpenAI話GPT-6 Astra解決咗個大問題，用咗$20M compute。但係researcher Tristan Buckmaster話佢自己嘅work被OpenAI偷咗，靠Codex同Claude磨出嚟嘅。OpenAI咁樣真係ok？wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: OpenAI announced on September 8th that GPT-6 Astra had solved a hard problem, costing $20 million in compute. Researcher Tristan Buckmaster says parts of OpenAI's approach look a lot like his own independent work, which he had been building with OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude. The ethics are ugly.
clips.source_hint: Researcher accuses OpenAI of lifting his work for the Astra breakthrough
clips.text_en_b2: On September 8th, OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Astra, claiming it cracked a notoriously hard problem after burning through $20 million in compute. Almost immediately, researcher Tristan Buckmaster pointed out that chunks of the approach bear a striking resemblance to his own independent work, which he had been painstakingly building with OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude. The ethics here are genuinely murky. Whether OpenAI crossed a line or simply converged on similar solutions is now fueling heated debate across the AI community.
clips.text_en_c1: On the eighth of September, OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Astra, claiming the model had resolved an intractable problem at a computational cost exceeding twenty million dollars. Almost immediately, independent researcher Tristan Buckmaster observed striking similarities between Astra's architecture and his own unpublished methodology, which he had been iteratively refining using OpenAI Codex and Anthropic's Claude. Whether the resemblance reflects convergent discovery, conscious appropriation, or something more ambiguous remains contested, though the optics, as far as the research community is concerned, are unambiguously grotesque.
clips.text_en_c2: On the eighth of September, OpenAI publicly announced that its forthcoming GPT-6 Astra had resolved a notoriously intractable problem, allegedly at the cost of some twenty million dollars in compute. Almost immediately, independent researcher Tristan Buckmaster observed that certain elements of the breakthrough bear an uncanny resemblance to work he had been developing himself, tooling his experiments with OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude in tandem. Whether this constitutes outright appropriation or merely convergent insight is, of course, the question that animates every such controversy. What remains disquieting is the asymmetry of resources: a lone researcher, however gifted, is scarcely equipped to contest a corporation with an institutional memory that conveniently runs on its own terms.

clips.text_zh: OECD PISA新study，760K個學生、91個國家，全球數學同閱讀分數一直跌，只有中國係升。中國average kid 612分，已經係其他國家嘅「精英」水平。跟住啦香港。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: New OECD PISA study of 760,000 students across 91 countries. Global math and reading scores are cratering everywhere except China. The elite level in math starts at 607, and the average Chinese kid scores 612. A normal Chinese student is at what the rest of the world calls top performer.
clips.source_hint: Anons posting about China dominating PISA
clips.text_en_b2: The latest OECD PISA study, covering roughly 760,000 students across 91 countries, confirms a troubling global trend: math and reading scores are plummeting almost everywhere. China, however, is moving in the opposite direction. The average Chinese student scored 612 in math, which is comfortably above the elite threshold of 607, a benchmark most other countries reserve for their top performers. In other words, what counts as exceptional talent elsewhere is the baseline in China. Hong Kong appears to be following suit.
clips.text_en_c1: The latest OECD PISA assessment, encompassing 760,000 students across ninety-one nations, paints a rather disquieting portrait of global educational decline: mathematics and reading literacy have plummeted virtually everywhere, save for one conspicuous outlier. While the threshold designating elite mathematical performance sits at 607, the average Chinese student now attains 612, meaning a typical pupil in Shanghai or Beijing outscores what the remainder of the world considers its finest. Hong Kong, predictably, has climbed alongside the mainland, a development that should occasion sober reflection rather than reflexive triumphalism.
clips.text_en_c2: The most recent OECD PISA study, encompassing roughly 760,000 students across ninety-one countries, has delivered a sobering verdict on the state of global education. Reading and mathematics scores have declined precipitously almost everywhere, with one conspicuous exception. China, alone among the surveyed nations, has registered an upward trajectory, its average student attaining 612 points in mathematics, a figure that, by the study's own metrics, qualifies as elite performance, since the elite threshold commences at 607. In effect, the median Chinese pupil now outperforms what the remainder of the world would consider its top tier. Hong Kong, predictably, is being invoked as the regional exemplar, and the policy implications are unlikely to be lost on ministries of education anywhere.

clips.text_zh: 暴雪班worker贏咗個歷史性union contract，可能會成個game industry嘅新standard。連AAA studio都識搞工會，lol。打機嘅未來唔止AI搞你，連老細都搞唔到你。btw我support。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Blizzard workers just won a historic union contract that could set a new standard across the game industry. /v/ is hyped, calling it Blizzard coming back after years of bad PR. The contract covers pay, AI rules, and crunch protections for developers.
clips.text_en_b2: Blizzard workers have just secured a historic union contract, and /v/ is losing its mind, framing it as the company's redemption arc after years of brutal PR disasters. The deal covers pay, lays down firm rules around AI usage, and finally puts proper crunch protections in place for developers. Because Blizzard remains an AAA studio, the agreement could easily ripple outward and become the new industry standard.
clips.text_en_c1: Blizzard's workforce has ratified a landmark union contract, the first of its kind at a major AAA studio, an outcome that may well establish a template for the remainder of the games industry. /v/, having endured years of corporate missteps, is cautiously celebrating what some are calling a genuine reputational turning point. The agreement addresses compensation, establishes meaningful guardrails against AI displacement, and enshrines concrete protections against the crunch culture that has historically defined production cycles here.
clips.text_en_c2: In what may yet prove a watershed moment for the industry, Blizzard's workforce has ratified a historic collective-bargaining agreement whose provisions could plausibly establish a new benchmark for AAA studios worldwide. The contract addresses compensation, imposes substantive constraints on the deployment of generative AI, and enshrines meaningful protections against the notorious crunch culture that has long defined game development. Reaction on /v/ has been euphoric, with users framing the agreement as evidence that the venerable Blizzard of old, so battered by years of reputational damage, may yet stage a redemption of sorts. Should the model prove durable, the implications extend well beyond any single studio, signalling that even the most storied publishers are no longer immune to the demands of organised labour.

clips.text_zh: 個post話calories in calories out根本唔解釋點解你會肥，同問Elon點解有錢然後答「因為收入多過支出」一樣廢。1pl8 OHP仲遠過2pl8 bench，thx睇完繼續gym。
clips.text_en_b1: An anon on /fit/ argues that calories in calories out is a tautology, like asking why Musk is rich and answering 'he spent less than he earned'. It doesn't explain why fat gain happens. Other anons are still posting lifts, one says he's closer to a 1-plate OHP than a 2-plate bench.
clips.source_hint: Anons argue about CICO and post their lifts
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /fit/ dropped a scorching take arguing that calories in, calories out is essentially a tautology, essentially asking why Elon Musk is wealthy and answering 'because he earns more than he spends.' It explains nothing about the actual mechanism of fat accumulation. Other anons brushed it off and kept posting their lifts. One lifter noted sheepishly that a 1-plate overhead press still feels further away than a 2-plate bench press. The thread carried on regardless.
clips.text_en_c1: A particularly sharp anon on /fit/ has taken it upon himself to demolish the calories-in-calories-out framework, arguing convincingly that the doctrine amounts to little more than circular reasoning, comparable to interrogating why Elon Musk is wealthy and accepting "because his income exceeded his expenditure" as a satisfactory explanation. The model, he contends, entirely fails to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of adipose accumulation. Meanwhile, the thread has devolved into the customary lift-spam, with one user lamenting that a single-plate overhead press remains tantalisingly closer than a two-plate bench.
clips.text_en_c2: A provocative poster on /fit/ has reignited a venerable debate by contending that the calories-in-calories-out paradigm, otherwise known as CICO, is little more than a circular tautology. To explain corpulence by appeal to caloric arithmetic, the argument runs, is rather like explaining Elon Musk's fortune by observing that his income has exceeded his expenditure; the statement is technically unimpeachable yet explanatorily vacuous. The thread, characteristically, has bifurcated into metaphysics and logistics, with one dissenter noting, between sets of a workout, that a one-plate overhead press remains a more distant prospect than a two-plate bench press. Gyms, it seems, continue to function irrespective of epistemological disputes.

clips.text_en_b1: Puella Madoka Magica: Walpurgis no Kaiten interview raws are out, plus the manga adaptation volume 01 just dropped. Seiyuu Chiwa Saito (Homura) even said Muhdoka is Homura's first love. /a/ is melting over the new lore and the Homura backstory hints.

clips.text_en_b2: Fresh material for Puella Madoka Magica: Walpurgis no Kaiten has surfaced, including interview raws and the manga adaptation's first volume. In one interview, seiyuu Chiwa Saito, the voice of Homura, dropped the bombshell that Madoka is Homura's first love, sending /a/ into absolute meltdown. Fans are poring over every line for backstory hints about Homura's arc. The combination of new lore and emotional weight has the thread buzzing with speculation about where the story might head next.
clips.text_en_c1: Fresh materials for Puella Madoka Magica: Walpurgis no Kaiten have surfaced, including raw interview transcripts alongside the inaugural volume of the manga adaptation, which dropped earlier this week. In a particularly poignant revelation, Homura's voice actress Chiwa Saito disclosed that Madoka constitutes Homura's inaugural experience of romantic love, a detail that has predictably unravelled the already fragile composure of /a/. The community is now dissecting every frame for further Homura backstory fragments, and the prevailing sentiment appears to be one of exquisite, if restrained, devastation.
clips.text_en_c2: Fresh materials have surfaced for Puella Magoka Magica: Walpurgis no Kaiten, with raw interview transcripts circulating alongside the inaugural volume of the manga adaptation, much to the evident delirium of /a/. Among the more affecting revelations is a comment attributed to Chiwa Saitō, the seiyū whose voice has lent Homura its singular pathos, in which she characterises Madoka as Homura's first love. The remark, whether scripted or extemporised, has provoked an outpouring of conspicuous anguish across the thread, with users mining the new lore for corroboration of Homura's long-suspected emotional devastation. Such disclosures, however sparingly issued, appear to function as accelerants upon a fandom already predisposed to romantic catastrophism.
